input: nums is a Array of n integers with 0 <= n <= 4294967295. Values lie in [-9007199254740990, 9007199254740990], one unit inside the safe-integer endpoints; duplicates and arbitrary order are accepted. String inputs, when present, are primitive strings, not boxed strings. Integer values are primitive safe-integer Number, excluding negative zero, NaN, infinities, fractions and BigInt. Arrays are dense ordinary Arrays, not sparse arrays, proxies, subclasses or accessor-backed collections. There is no concurrent mutation or monkey-patching of standard built-ins. Preconditions are not checked at runtime. Allocation and runtime resource limits still require qualification; this declared domain is not a capacity or completion guarantee.
return: The length of the longest run of consecutive distinct integer values present anywhere in nums, regardless of input order. Duplicate occurrences do not extend a run. Empty input returns 0; only the length is returned, not an ordered Array.
mutation_aliasing: All inputs, their ordering and caller-owned containers remain unchanged. The Solution instance retains no state, and separate calls share no mutable result state. A fresh private set deduplicates values. Its iteration order may differ across languages, but only an order-independent maximum length is returned.
numeric: The one-unit margin makes value - 1 and current + 1 exact safe integers even at input extremes. Every successful increment reaches another admitted input value, so current remains inside the margin. Run lengths and indices are bounded by n. Full safe-endpoint inputs are deliberately outside this author-declared paired domain until an endpoint-aware variant is separately qualified.
complexity: O(n + 1) set insertions/membership operations and O(n + 1) retained set space. Only a value lacking its predecessor starts a run, so successful successor steps total at most the number of distinct values. This gives expected O(n + 1) time under average O(1) hash-set operations; adversarial collision/runtime guarantees are separate and not claimed. JavaScript Set complexity must be qualified for the runtime: ECMAScript does not promise universal constant-time operations. No sorting is used.
source_accounting: The complete standalone source is 411 UTF-8 bytes, including the Solution class, method signature, every loop, condition, allocation, standard built-in call, annotation/comment where present, whitespace and terminal newline. There are no custom helper definitions, imports, generated implementations or hidden source expansion. Built-in operations are not free: their allocations and work are included in the stated runtime/storage costs. TreeNode, where used, is an explicit caller-owned input shape and no node is constructed. Any eventual judge-interface adapter is additional charged source; method-style interface parity with frozen sources remains unqualified.
